The game is good; you can play for a whole day and, when taking a break, realize how long you have been playing.

In terms of gameplay, it is simple: you command a submarine, sink ships, and manage the crew. It feels like This War of Mine in a submarine; it's good.

For combat, this game takes a very realistic approach; one depth charge is enough to sink you. So, keep moving, use the seabed for cover, and deploy decoys to escape. A hull breach in this game can flood a section of the sub in less than 2 minutes, which is not enough time to have a mechanic fix the leak. This can be frustrating when you are detected.

For missions, you can deploy a landing party to sabotage a railway or drop a spy on an enemy coast. There is not a large variety because you play as a sub, and in WWII, the main mission for subs was simply to sink merchants carrying cargo. The other types of missions are secondary, and this can feel tedious, particularly in a campaign starting in 1939.

Regarding the types of subs, with the latest DLC, you can play with all types of U-boats that actually participated in WWII. With the "milk cows", you can have fun doing a Caribbean patrol with a Type VIIC or a Cape of Good Hope patrol with a Type IX.

As for bugs, crashes, and similar problems, they exist and can break the gameplay. Sometimes it feels like the devs either don't care or don't have the time to fix them.

This game was launched in Early Access in 2019, and since then, some bugs have persisted. However, the evolution of the game, even if slow, shows that the dev team is keen on keeping it alive. They will keep it updated and packed with extra content; for example, the Elektroboats Types XXI and XXIII will come, but it will take time until they arrive.

For those who have played the Silent Hunter series, this game adopts a more simulation-heavy, crew-managing style rather than being purely combat-oriented. Since this is a small dev team, with patience and time, the game will have as much content and detail as the later Silent Hunter games, if not more. A good example is the Laconia incident, where in UBOAT, you help rescue as many people as the boat can hold.

The modding community is alive, and the developers have implemented some mods into the vanilla game, which shows they are committed and open to suggestions and requests.

I have been playing the game since day one, and I highly recommend it to anyone interested in a submarine simulator where managing the crew is just as important as sinking ships.

The Exceptional:
1.	Tons of unique and beautiful port options from which to base and raid.
2.	Lots of convoy lanes and stunning ship types with sensible spawn rates.
3.	Variety and flexibility in missions, items, cargo, stats, medals and achievements. Enough to satisfy a submarine enthusiast.
4.	A truly dynamic campaign that involves you with transmissions while at sea, video briefings at port, and welcomes from the individual port commanders.
5.	A U-Boat that feels like it has depth in both management and first-person usage.
The Good:
1.	On lower AI difficulties, this game is a stellar arcade/first-person U-Boat sim for casual players and subsim enthusiasts alike.
2.	On higher AI difficulties, this game forces distinctly different choices: Not every spotted opportunity is worth the risk, screens are carefully entered, targets are limited to two or three ships per sweep, and being spotted forces an immediate underwater chase. And your eye is always on the clock for oxygen.
3.	The technology tree is impactful and it progresses sensibly on its own, though can speed up for those willing to invest.
4.	Torpedo maintenance is uncomplicated and auto-managed, though the chance of duds is always a real one.
5.	The orders screen is a vital component and works like a dream come true in most situations.
6.	The map is an incredible mix of navigational ease and historical information.
7.	Stuck out at sea without fuel? Call of milk cow! You’ll get your fuel and your torpedoes.
8.	External torpedo storage! And it works fine in first-person, too!
The Bad:
1.	Did your crew just get back from their three week vacation? Well, welcome back to a 15-bomber air raid in 1940! Courtesy of La Rochelle, Brest, and other cool ports.
2.	Welcome home from La Spezia port, kameraden! We know high command just told you to pass through the Strait of Gibraltar, but they want you to go back to Italy again. It’s no big deal, right? You’ve done it once already!
3.	Did you report that funnel smoke or ship you just spotted? Well, don’t worry! As you busy yourself with your deck gun, your friendly neighborhood U-058 will swoop in and launch 4 torpedoes at it too! But from the side of the ship you’ve pulled up on. Good luck with those four new holes in your boat!
4.	Bugs. To be fair, Deep Water Studio is a small studio. But I remember when I first got this game when it came out: The difficulty was with everything from performance, to time compression, to running the ship aground or off pathing during time compression, to missions getting stuck, etc etc etc. This has all been patched. I seriously commend the developers. But with the dawn of the new dlc, we are still dealing with the fallout months after. The glowing purple eyes glitch was endearing. But the numerous times my submarine has attempted to fire a torpedo at exactly 180 degrees and instead did an out-of-water barrel roll? Admittedly this bug, the save bug, and some other bugs have caused me to put this game down a few times until they were fixed. I accept this as the price of progress, but it is a factor of playing this game and it must be accepted.
The Ugly:
1.	On the highest AI difficulty, this game is unplayable. Corvettes will spot you creeping through a convoy screen while your periscope is barely above the waterline. They will then pursue you with ASDIC down to 200 meters depth with pinpoint accuracy. They have unlimited depth charges. And they don’t care about the convoy they have been attached to or its timetable; They will leave it behind. You cannot hide against the background of the ocean floor either, they will spot you and depth charge you over and over again. Thermal layers of water do not phase these rookies. All of this in 1939, which makes the shallower waters of the early game unnecessarily punishing. Whatever difficulty this is, it is far from historical and much closer to nonsensical.
2.	Crew management completely breaks down at the most critical of moments: During major underwater flooding. Even if every officer has a rebreather and parts, and you have 4 engineers aboard, the crew will just wander around the ship doing whatever they see fit to do. They will open bulkheads you want closed and let water in. They will close bulkheads you want open and let the water pressure build up until no one can open it. They will also open bulkheads and get in the way by carrying sailors to bunks, but the sailors cannot be tended to because the bunks are flooded. You have to go to the crew management screen just to deprioritize medical treatment. However, this feels like it should be an order instead: Prioritize the boat. Or something to that effect.

Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone interested in submarines. It has its flaws, but its boons far outweigh them. It is easily the best subsim game out there on the market right now. Especially for WW2.

[h1]Review zu UBOAT[/h1]

Auf UBOAT wurde ich vor allem durch meine Begeisterung für den Film „Das Boot“ (1981) aufmerksam. Für mich ist Das Boot bis heute der beste deutsche Film überhaupt. Die beklemmende Atmosphäre, das Leben an Bord und die ständige Anspannung unter Wasser haben mich schon immer fasziniert. Selbst als Kind. Schließlich war ich auch schon im originalen U-Boot, dass man damals für den Dreh verwendet hatte. Diesen metallsichen Geschmack auf meiner Zunge, während man sich wie eine Ölsardine in der Dose fühlt werde ich wohl niemals vergessen. Genau deshalb wollte ich wissen, wie gut ein modernes U-Boot-Spiel diese Stimmung einfangen kann.

Mein bisheriger Vergleichspunkt im U-Boot-Genre war lediglich das Spiel "Das Boot: German U-Boat Simulation", das ich vor einiger Zeit über GOG ausprobiert hatte. Entsprechend ging ich mit relativ wenig Genre-Erfahrung, aber hohen Erwartungen an UBOAT heran.

UBOAT versteht sich nicht als reine U-Boot-Simulation. Stattdessen kombiniert das Spiel klassische Simulationselemente mit Crew-Management, Ressourcenverwaltung und einer Art Rollenspielsystem für die Besatzung.

Das bedeutet, dass man nicht nur Torpedos abschießt und Schiffe versenkt, sondern sich auch um die Mannschaft kümmern muss. Matrosen werden müde, Offiziere benötigen Aufgaben und die Versorgung des Bootes spielt ebenfalls eine wichtige Rolle.
Diese Mischung macht UBOAT zugänglicher als viele ältere Simulationen, ohne dabei vollständig auf Realismus zu verzichten.

Die größte Stärke von UBOAT ist für mich ganz klar die Atmosphäre.
Bereits beim ersten Betreten des Bootes fallen zahlreiche Details auf, die Fans von Das Boot sofort bekannt vorkommen dürften. Das U-Boot selbst orientiert sich sehr stark an dem berühmten Boot aus dem Film. (Tatsächlich gibt es sogar den genauen Boottyp aus dem Film. Dieser ist zwar nicht ganz akurat dargestellt, aber nah genug dran) Die engen Gänge, die Anordnung der Räume und die allgemeine Gestaltung vermitteln schnell das Gefühl, tatsächlich Teil einer Besatzung zu sein. Ins Besondere wenn man in der Egoperspektive spielt.

Dazu kommt die hervorragende Musik. Der Soundtrack unterstützt die Stimmung ausgezeichnet und schafft es, ruhige Patrouillen ebenso zu begleiten wie hektische Gefechtssituationen.

Besonders positiv sind zudem die vielen kleinen Details, die das Leben an Bord glaubwürdig wirken lassen. Ein schönes Beispiel ist das Verhalten der Besatzung beim Durchqueren von Luken. Rennen Crewmitglieder durch eine Luke, greifen sie automatisch nach den Haltegriffen oberhalb der Öffnung. Solche Kleinigkeiten haben keinen spielerischen Nutzen, tragen aber enorm zur Immersion bei.

Die eigentlichen Einsätze bestehen häufig aus langen Patrouillen, Aufklärungsfahrten und Angriffen auf feindliche Schiffe oder Konvois.

Wer Action im Minutentakt erwartet, dürfte zunächst überrascht sein: Ein großer Teil des Spiels besteht aus Planung, Navigation und Beobachtung. Das passt allerdings hervorragend zum Thema.

Besonders befriedigend sind erfolgreiche Torpedoangriffe. Wenn nach längerer Vorbereitung ein Torpedo sein Ziel trifft und ein feindliches Schiff langsam im Meer versinkt, entsteht ein Erfolgserlebnis, das viele andere Simulationsspiele nur selten erreichen. Ich liebe auch das Katz- und Mausspiel mit Zerstörern und das man feindliche Schiffe vom Typ her erst klassifizieren sollte, um seine Torpedos letztendlich nicht zu verschwenden.

Trotz aller Stärken ist UBOAT nicht frei von Problemen.
Gerade die KI verhält sich gelegentlich merkwürdig. Besatzungsmitglieder treffen nicht immer nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen oder bleiben an bestimmten Aufgaben hängen. Auch Pathfinding-Probleme können auftreten.

Darüber hinaus bewegt sich UBOAT manchmal etwas unsicher zwischen Hardcore-Simulation und Managementspiel. Manche Systeme sind sehr detailliert, andere wirken vergleichsweise vereinfacht. Das sorgt gelegentlich für ein unausgewogenes Gesamtbild. Allerdings ist das Spiel hierbei tatsächlich sehr kulant und man kann seinen Schwierigkeitsgrad recht detailliert selbst einstellen.

Auch technisch war das Spiel insbesondere während seiner Early-Access-Phase nicht immer frei von Bugs. Viele davon wurden inzwischen behoben, dennoch trifft man gelegentlich noch auf kleinere Ungereimtheiten.

Verglichen mit dem älteren Das Boot: German U-Boat Simulation wirkt UBOAT deutlich moderner, zugänglicher und atmosphärischer.
Während ältere U-Boot-Simulationen häufig stark auf technische Genauigkeit und komplexe Bedienung setzten, versucht UBOAT einen Mittelweg zu finden. Das macht den Einstieg deutlich angenehmer, ohne den Reiz des Kommandierens eines U-Boots vollständig zu verlieren.
Wer keine jahrelange Erfahrung mit Simulationsspielen besitzt, dürfte mit UBOAT wesentlich schneller zurechtkommen.

[h3]Gutes & Schlechtes:[/h3]

[u][b]Pro:[/b][/u]

+ Hervorragende Atmosphäre und gute Immersion
+ Stark von Das Boot inspirierte Präsentation
+ Ein gewisser U-Boot-Typ ist sehr nah am berühmten Filmboot aus dem Film gestaltet worden
+ Ausgezeichneter Soundtrack
+ Viele liebevolle Details
+ Glaubwürdiges Leben an Bord
+ Gelungene Mischung aus Simulation und Management
+ Spannende Torpedoangriffe
+ Zugänglicher als viele ältere U-Boot-Simulationen. Das ist mir mir besonders im direkten Vergleich mit "Das Boot: German U-Boat Simulation" aufgefallen

[u][b]Contra:[/b][/u]

- Gelegentliche KI-Probleme
- Vereinzelte Bugs und technische Ungereimtheiten
- Manche Management-Aufgaben können repetitiv werden
- Nicht alle Systeme wirken gleich tief ausgearbeitet
- Wenig geeignet für Spieler, die permanente Action erwarten

[u][b]Prontra:[/b][/u]

+- Langsames Spieltempo
+- Hoher Fokus auf Planung und Beobachtung
+- Mischung aus Simulation und Management ist Geschmackssache

UBOAT hat für mich etwas geschafft, das nur wenige Spiele erreichen: Es vermittelt zumindest ansatzweise das Gefühl, Teil der Besatzung aus Das Boot zu sein. Als großer Fan des Films war genau das der Hauptgrund, warum ich das Spiel überhaupt ausprobiert habe, und in dieser Hinsicht wurde ich nicht enttäuscht.

Besonders die Atmosphäre, die Musik, die detailreiche Nachbildung der verschiedenen U-Boot-Typen und die vielen kleinen Animationen an Bord tragen erheblich dazu bei. Wenn Matrosen durch Luken sprinten und sich dabei automatisch an den Griffen festhalten, merkt man, wie viel Liebe zum Detail in das Projekt geflossen ist.

Zwar besitzt UBOAT einige technische Schwächen und die KI sorgt gelegentlich für Frust, insgesamt bietet das Spiel jedoch eine überzeugende Mischung aus Simulation, Management und Atmosphäre. Für Fans von Das Boot, U-Boot-Geschichte oder maritimen Simulationen ist UBOAT deshalb eine klare Empfehlung und für mich bislang die mit Abstand gelungenste U-Boot-Erfahrung, die ich gespielt habe. (Auch wenn das natürlich nicht viel heißen mag, denn die bisherige Anzahl ist Zwei.)

Ich danke fürs Lesen und wünsche sehr viel Spaß beim Spielen! ;-)

I REALLY wanted to like this game, it brings fond memories of the hours I spent playing Silent Service as a kid, and the emotions of some great movies like Das Boot. But, it just doesn't feel like it's a finished product. The controls are not intuitive, nor are they always functional. When I hit "pause", some part of me expects the game to... well, pause. And it USUALLY does, just not every time. The time lapse/compression feature is nice, but when trying to collect crates of tires from the wreckage of one of the early missions, it would take 4 in-game days, and absolutely nothing I did could speed that up. Most menu/dialogue navigation during the tutorial took several more steps to complete than should be necessary - and while that's a small thing, it was actually a warning sign of the lack of polish I'd be experiencing throughout my game play. Volume, especially the voice acting, is very low. And using British accented English speakers to portray German sailors was an odd decision. Character creation would not allow me to change the voice type on my captain. I've had multiple freezes, with the latest one locking up my entire system. There are typos/grammar issues in the subtitles. The developer constantly fiddles with the price (generally around $30 USD), so it would appear to be on sale in spite of still being about $30 USD, so take a moment to check that carefully before blindly hitting Buy.

Taking the time to line up a 3 torpedo salvo on a broadside destroyer, watching them close on the clueless enemy, and then seeing *HIT!* *HIT!* *MISS!* followed by their ship sinking into the deep blue sea is SO INCREDIBLY rewarding! But then nothing would allow me to target the trawler it was escorting! I had to surface and manually sink it with my deck gun (and taking some damage from their own deck gun).

I've got 10 hours in, and bought this on sale, so it's going to stay in my library. I'm hoping that they spend some time, money, and effort fixing it instead of releasing DLC boats in the future, because I REALLY want to like this game, and it makes me really sad that I don't. :(

After about 100 hours of time spent in the dangerous waters of the Atlantic since Uboat's time in early access I have to say. 

Not bad...

Its a perfectly serviceable and impressive title. When you consider it was made by only 4 people and is a love letter to the classics of the subsim genre like the Silent Hunter series it feels like it has achieved that vision, almost. Uboat is far from perfect whether its constant bugs, a clunky UI and AI, and some very questionable choices for those of us who prefer 90% realism, it kind of just bogs you down after a while. 

I so desperately wanted this game to be amazing and after a lot of time beating my head against the wall I've personally decided to shelve it until some things change. I've had so many great moments ruined by the clunky systems in game that it just doesn't feel worth it to play just to end up frustrated. For example there is a mission where you sneak into the harbor of Scapa Flow to destroy a British warship. Its based on historical precedent and is available fairly early in game circa 1939-1940, While it offers a fun challenge its certainly not great when you get there and realize that using full realism with the torpedo calculator (manually setting range, AOB, and speed) there is no way to set your torpedo's between impact and magnetic in full manual. INSTEAD you have to use the UI from the periscope and change the setting there and that completely kills the immersion. 

I know that this sounds nitpicky but if the game wants to allow you the full realism experience why is something as basic as this available not on the TDC (where it should be). In short the little issues with this game really start to add up and this game is already slow and methodical to begin with so it beats you down. While some supporters with rose tinted Kriegsmarine glasses pretend these issues don't matter they do and by pretending you just make it all the more obvious that the game is never going to be as good as Silent Hunter 3 so why bother?
